_note: Cutaway schematics. A reactor is a system rather than an object, so each prompt names the one piece of geometry that tells this design apart from its neighbours (rod drives from below on a BWR, horizontal pressure tubes on a CANDU, non-planar coils on a stellarator). The house style bans labels, so the silhouette has to carry the identification on its own.

prompts.1: Cutaway schematic of a pressurized water reactor: a tall cylindrical steel pressure vessel with a domed head and a dense bundle of square fuel assemblies inside, a forest of thin control rod drive shafts entering through the top head, and two large pipes looping sideways to a much taller vertical U-tube steam generator standing beside it with a bulbous upper section, plus a squat coolant pump on the return leg. Water paths shown as muted steel-blue.
prompts.2: Cutaway schematic of a boiling water reactor: one bulbous steel pressure vessel doing the whole job, with fuel assemblies in the lower third, tall stacked steam separator standpipes and a flat dryer bank filling the upper dome, a single large steam pipe leaving the top side, and the distinguishing feature clearly drawn: many control rod drive housings entering through the BOTTOM head from underneath. Steam paths muted steel-blue.
prompts.3: Cutaway schematic of a VVER reactor: a vertical cylindrical pressure vessel holding hexagonal fuel assemblies, connected by two thick pipes to a large HORIZONTAL cylindrical steam generator lying on its side beside the vessel, roughly as long as the vessel is tall. The horizontal steam generator is the point of the drawing and should dominate the right half.
prompts.4: Cutaway schematic of a small modular light-water reactor: one slim tall integral pressure vessel containing the small core at the bottom and helical coil steam generators wrapped inside the upper part of the same vessel, with no external loop piping at all, the whole module standing submerged in a deep water-filled concrete pool below ground level. Emphasize how slender and self-contained the module is.
prompts.5: Cutaway schematic of a CANDU heavy-water reactor: a large HORIZONTAL cylindrical calandria drum shown end-on-three-quarter, pierced through by a regular grid of hundreds of horizontal pressure tubes running its full length, with a fuelling machine on a carriage docked to the tube face at one end. The horizontal tube lattice is the subject.
prompts.6: Cutaway schematic of an RBMK reactor: a very wide squat stack of rectangular graphite blocks forming a massive cube, pierced by a regular grid of vertical fuel channel tubes, topped by a floor of round channel cap plates, with a large gantry refuelling machine on rails above. Emphasize the great width and the graphite block masonry.
prompts.7: Cutaway schematic of a gas-cooled Magnox or AGR reactor: a very thick squat concrete pressure vessel drawn in section, containing a cylindrical graphite core in the middle and, uniquely, the boilers and gas circulators standing inside the same concrete vessel in the annulus around the core. CO2 gas flow arrows as muted steel-blue.
prompts.8: Cutaway schematic of a pebble-bed high-temperature reactor: a vertical cylindrical vessel packed full of thousands of small spheres, the bed narrowing into a conical hopper at the bottom that funnels into a single discharge chute pipe, with a return pipe carrying spheres back up to the top. Helium ducts leave the side. The mass of individual spheres is the subject.
prompts.9: Cutaway schematic of a prismatic high-temperature gas reactor: a vertical vessel containing a neat stacked array of large hexagonal graphite blocks forming columns, each block face showing a pattern of round vertical coolant channels drilled through it, helium ducts entering and leaving the side. The hexagonal block columns are the subject.
prompts.10: Cutaway schematic of a pool-type sodium-cooled fast reactor: a wide squat cylindrical tank with a flat roof deck, filled with liquid sodium whose free surface is clearly drawn as a muted steel-blue level line, and everything submerged in that pool: a small compact core low in the tank, two intermediate heat exchangers, and two tall vertical pump columns hanging from the deck. No tall vessel, no external loop.
prompts.11: Cutaway schematic of a lead-cooled fast reactor: a heavy squat pool vessel with visibly thick walls, filled with dense molten lead shown with a heavy dark liquid surface line, a small compact core near the bottom, and steam generators immersed directly in the lead. Draw it noticeably more massive and thick-walled than a sodium reactor.
prompts.12: Cutaway schematic of a helium-cooled gas fast reactor: a compact vertical pressure vessel with a small dense fast core and no moderator, connected by two large-diameter gas ducts to a horizontal turbomachine module beside it. The very large duct diameter relative to the small core is the identifying feature.
prompts.13: Cutaway schematic of a thermal molten salt reactor with liquid fuel: a vessel containing a lattice of hexagonal graphite moderator blocks with channels through which liquid fuel salt flows, a pump and heat exchanger in an external salt loop, and below the vessel a drain tank connected by a short vertical pipe with a freeze plug at its neck. Salt paths as muted steel-blue.
prompts.14: Cutaway schematic of a fast-spectrum molten salt reactor: a plain smooth-walled cylindrical vessel with no internal structure at all, just circulating liquid salt, connected to an external loop with a salt pump and a heat exchanger. The empty, uncluttered core is the identifying feature; contrast it with a graphite-filled core.
prompts.15: Cutaway schematic of a two-fluid thorium molten salt breeder: a vessel drawn in section showing an inner fuel salt core region surrounded by a separate concentric outer blanket salt annulus, the two liquids kept apart by a barrier wall, with a small chemical processing skid of tanks and columns connected beside it. The nested core-inside-blanket geometry is the subject.
prompts.16: Cutaway schematic of a fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactor: a vessel filled with clear liquid salt shown as a translucent muted steel-blue volume, with solid spherical fuel pebbles suspended and floating within the liquid rather than in a dry packed bed, and a salt loop leaving the side. Pebbles in liquid is the point.
prompts.17: Cutaway schematic of a microreactor as a transportable product: a small sealed reactor module sized like a shipping container, mounted on a low transport skid with lifting lugs, its end wall cut away to show a compact core and a heat exchanger inside. Emphasize the shipping-container proportions and the total absence of a plant around it.
prompts.18: Cutaway schematic of a space heat-pipe reactor: a small squat cylindrical core at the bottom with a bundle of slender heat pipes running vertically out of it into a conical shield, above which large flat radiator panels fan outward in a wide skirt. Slim, spacecraft-like proportions on a plain background.
prompts.19: Cutaway schematic of a naval propulsion reactor: a section of a submarine pressure hull cylinder cut away to reveal a very compact pressure vessel and a close-coupled steam generator packed tightly into the hull with almost no clearance, plus a turbine and reduction gear aft driving a shaft. Emphasize how tightly everything is packed into the round hull.
prompts.20: Cutaway schematic of a tokamak: a doughnut-shaped vacuum vessel with a wedge cut away to reveal a glowing muted steel-blue ring of plasma inside, encircled by a ring of large D-shaped toroidal field coils, plus a tall central solenoid column running up the middle of the doughnut hole. Symmetrical and regular.
prompts.21: Cutaway schematic of a stellarator: a set of five or six wildly twisted non-planar modular coils, each a different contorted three-dimensional shape, wrapped around a bean-shaped plasma volume that twists as it goes around the torus. The irregular, hand-warped coil geometry is the identifying feature and should look deliberately unlike a tokamak's clean D-coils.
prompts.22: Cutaway schematic of a laser inertial confinement fusion chamber: a large hollow sphere with a regular pattern of many round beam port tubes over its whole surface, all aimed inward, with thin converging beam lines drawn meeting at a single tiny capsule suspended at the exact center on a thin holder arm.
prompts.23: Cutaway schematic of a magnetized target fusion machine: a spherical chamber ringed by a dense radial array of large pneumatic ram pistons all pointing inward at the center, with a swirling liquid metal vortex liner inside the chamber and a plasma injector entering along the axis.
prompts.24: Cutaway schematic of a field-reversed configuration device: a long straight horizontal cylindrical vacuum chamber with a formation section at each end, ringed by simple circular coils along its whole length, and two smoke-ring-shaped plasma toroids drawn mid-flight travelling inward toward a merging point at the center. Straight and axial, no torus anywhere.
prompts.25: Cutaway schematic of a Z-pinch pulsed-power machine: a large flat radial disk transmission line converging inward on a small central target region, where a cylindrical cage of very fine parallel wires stands between a top and bottom electrode. Show the huge radial disk feeding an almost invisibly small wire array at the hub.
